definition: A software system that uses a model, instructions, state, and tools to pursue a bounded objective.
AI capabilities and models managed by the browser or platform and exposed through APIs.
Inference performed on the user's device or browser.
An architecture combining client-side and server-side inference with routing and fallback.
The process of generating outputs from a trained model using new input.
Additional training that adapts an existing model to a repeated task, style, or domain.
Retrieval-augmented generation; supplying retrieved source content to a model at inference time.
A numeric vector representation used to compare semantic similarity.
The maximum amount of input and conversation state a model can process at once.
An unsupported or incorrect model-generated claim.
Untrusted instructions that attempt to override intended model or tool behavior.
A controlled alternate path used when the preferred model or environment is unavailable.
Selecting an execution path and model using task, risk, cost, privacy, and capability criteria.
The degree to which an output is supported by approved evidence.
